To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) agency risk in SOEs results in the agents' pursuit of quantity at the expense of novelty in innovation activities, (ii) corporate governance tools reduce such agency risk, and (iii) public governance quality enhances the effectiveness of such corporate governance tools.

1) SOE managers' private incentives, as reflected by their compensation, are positively related to the novelty of innovation; 2) SOEs with higher quality public governance have higher quality of corporate governance, which in turn is positively related to the quality of innovation; 3) the positive relationship between SOEs' quality of corporate governance and their quality of innovation is stronger in those SOEs with higher public governance quality.

(i) SOEs with high quality corporate governance tools and high quality public institutions are associated with higher innovation novelty and (ii) SOEs with higher quality public institutions have higher innovation novelty when their corporate governance tools are better aligned.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the agency risk in innovation activities, which is an important yet under-researched area, and provides new insights into the role of public and corporate governance in mitigating the agency risk in firm innovation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of corporate governance and public governance in SOEs has an important influence on the innovation activities in SOEs, and this effect is enhanced by the quality of public governance.
the quality of public governance is positively related to the quality of corporate governance in SOEs, which in turn is related to the quality and quantity of firm innovation.

the results of the research are not only consistent with the theoretical predictions, but also provide a more detailed understanding on the role of governance in innovation management, especially the role of public governance in corporate governance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
public governance, corporate governance, and firm innovation are intertwined.
we examine how agency risk in state-owned enterprises (SOEs), and the quality of both public and corporate governance, jointly affect the firm innovation.

the quality of both public and corporate governance is positively associated with the novelty of innovation activities in Chinese SOEs, but the effect of corporate governance is stronger than that of public governance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SOEs' innovation is more likely to be quantity-oriented than novelty-oriented, and the quality of both corporate and public governance is critical in mitigating such agency risk.
the quality of public governance is an important determinant of firm innovation, which has important implications for policy makers.
public governance can improve the functioning of corporate tools and thereby enhance firm innovation.
